title: SALT
subtitle: The Empire's Smallest Fear
intro: In 1930, the British Raj taxed the one thing every Indian could gather for free. One man picked up a handful of salt, and the Empire discovered a weapon it could not arrest.
lede: A 5:04 film in 40 scenes and 82 shots, built from 10 procedural sets, 40 sourced lines and 7 authored transitions. Every frame rendered on free GitHub Actions hardware.

stats.label: sourced lines
stats.note: every line carries a source id

cut.heading: 82 shots across 40 scenes.
cut.body: The final cut runs 5:04 at 24 fps; the average shot is 3.7 seconds. 75 of the 82 joins are hard cuts. The other 7 are authored transitions (page turn, paper wipe, iris, dip). The scene list below is generated from the release timeline, not the storyboard.

motion.heading: The edit has a grammar.
motion.body: The grammar is paper-ledger. The signature moves are listed below. Transition counts come from the final edit manifest.
signature: document reveal: the page moves before the camera does
page-turn wipe: a printed edge carries the next set in
stamp match: a rubber stamp lands where the last shot cut
ruling lines: horizontal rules become the horizon of the next set

families.name: Page turn
families.use: A page turns and the next set arrives on its back.

families.name: Paper wipe
families.use: A printed edge carries the next set into frame.

families.name: Iris
families.use: A lamp or valve closes to a circle, moving the eye to the next object.

families.name: Dip
families.use: A held gap between two arguments.

families.name: Hard cut
families.use: The default join. Used where softening would weaken the argument.

sources.heading: Every line has a source.
sources.body: The storyboard is validated before rendering. Each narration line carries a source id, and the render fails if the line, shot or source is missing. The counts below come from the final release timeline.

pipeline.heading: Every frame is assembled on GitHub.
pipeline.body: Blender, Piper, Chromium and ffmpeg run on a free Ubuntu CPU runner. The owner's machine writes the code; it does not render the film. The pipeline is public, repeatable and allowed to fail loudly.

items.title: Source lock
items.body: The storyboard is a JSON contract. Every narration line names a source. The validator refuses unsourced lines, missing shots and filler before a runner is allowed to render.

items.title: Procedural sets
items.body: Blender 4.2 builds the film's sets as still plates. No stock images.

items.title: Narration
items.body: Piper reads the script locally with en_US-lessac-medium. No cloud narration, no per-word billing, no API key in the repository.

items.title: Camera and type
items.body: Chromium drives the timeline frame by frame: push-ins, pans, match cuts, mask wipes, impact cards and captions. The camera is code, so every frame is repeatable.

items.title: Score and master
items.body: ffmpeg synthesises the score, mixes the narration, burns the SRT into the master and encodes the MP4.

items.title: Free CI
items.body: The render runs on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu CPU. No GPU. No paid runner. The owner's machine writes the code; it does not render the film.

record.heading: What the record shows.
record.body: Each entry is taken from the release itself: the timeline, the edit manifest and the independent QC report. A dossier that only shows the final cut is a portfolio, not a process.

items.title: Source lock
items.body: 40 narration lines across 5 sources. Every line in the final timeline resolves to a source in the release metadata; the validator refuses a line without one.

items.title: Final cut
items.body: 40 scenes, 82 shots, 5:04. Average shot 3.7s. 75 hard cuts and 7 authored transitions.

items.title: Independent QC
items.body: Passed: -1.2 dBTP wanted no higher than -1; I -12.9 LUFS wanted -16.5 to -11; median 45.6 dB wanted at least 36 dB, worst 42.0 dB at S03-L3; 108 cues in salt-march.srt; median edge/interior 1.17 wanted at most 1.75.

items.title: Release
items.body: Release film-salt-march-final-38 carries the 1080 master, SRT, thumbnail, timeline, edit manifest and script. The site deploys only the 720 preview.

build.heading: The render is public.
build.body: Recent Film pipeline runs, read from the public GitHub API. The workflow log is part of the record.

credits.heading: Who did what.
credits.body: The same free, local toolchain on every film: no paid API, no GPU and no stock footage.
rules: Every narration line carries a source id. The render fails if a line, shot or source is missing.
No number on screen without a source or an explicit attribution.
No stock footage. Every set is procedural.
No paid API keys. The pipeline runs on free CI.
If the edit is weak, the render does not ship.
credits.quote: “If the edit is weak, the render does not ship.”
credits.quoteNote: The 1080 master is published only after independent QC passes and the release is attached.

scenes.title: British Plinth
scenes.purpose: Chapter 1, line 1: Start with the mineral, then the argument for choosing it

narration.text: Salt. The British Empire could tax almost anything; it chose the one thing the poorest Indian could gather for free.

scenes.title: Constitution Plinth
scenes.purpose: Chapter 1, line 2: Start with the mineral, then the argument for choosing it

narration.text: A constitution could not be attacked directly; a tax on salt could.

scenes.title: Congress Desk
scenes.purpose: Chapter 1, line 3: Start with the mineral, then the argument for choosing it

narration.text: The Congress gave Gandhi the first act of civil disobedience, expecting his arrest.

scenes.title: White Flowing Water Sample
scenes.purpose: Chapter 1, line 4: Start with the mineral, then the argument for choosing it

narration.text: The march was called the White Flowing River, for the khadi the marchers wore.

scenes.title: Salt Administrator's Office
scenes.purpose: Chapter 2, line 1: The Act, the depots, and why his own committee doubted the choice

narration.text: The Salt Act of 1882 gave the Raj a monopoly on collection and manufacture. Salt was free on the coast. The law made it a crime to take it.

scenes.title: British India Family Record
scenes.purpose: Chapter 2, line 2: The Act, the depots, and why his own committee doubted the choice

narration.text: The tax was small at the till and enormous in a poor family's kitchen. By 1930 it was 8.2 percent of British India's tax revenue.

scenes.title: Even Nehru Card Catalogue
scenes.purpose: Chapter 2, line 3: The Act, the depots, and why his own committee doubted the choice

narration.text: Even Nehru was sceptical when Gandhi chose the salt tax.

scenes.title: Government Card Catalogue
scenes.purpose: Chapter 2, line 4: The Act, the depots, and why his own committee doubted the choice

narration.text: The Act limited all handling of salt to government depots.

scenes.title: Campaign Family Record
scenes.purpose: Chapter 2, line 5: The Act, the depots, and why his own committee doubted the choice

narration.text: Gandhi called the salt campaign a poor man's struggle.

scenes.title: Protect Indian Desk
scenes.purpose: Chapter 3, line 1: The eleven demands, the press prepared in advance, and a Viceroy who would not meet him

narration.text: On 2 March 1930, Gandhi wrote to the Viceroy with eleven demands. Abolish the salt tax. Cut military spending. Protect Indian cloth.

scenes.title: Lord Irwin Map Table
scenes.purpose: Chapter 3, line 2: The eleven demands, the press prepared in advance, and a Viceroy who would not meet him

narration.text: Lord Irwin was not impressed. He wrote to London that a salt campaign did not keep him awake at night.

scenes.title: Included Desk
scenes.purpose: Chapter 3, line 3: The eleven demands, the press prepared in advance, and a Viceroy who would not meet him

narration.text: The demands included land revenue relief, military cuts and a tariff on foreign cloth.

scenes.title: Briefed Corridor
scenes.purpose: Chapter 3, line 4: The eleven demands, the press prepared in advance, and a Viceroy who would not meet him

narration.text: Gandhi briefed the world's press before he left the ashram.

scenes.title: Ignored Letter
scenes.purpose: Chapter 3, line 5: The eleven demands, the press prepared in advance, and a Viceroy who would not meet him

narration.text: Irwin ignored the letter and refused to meet him before the march.

scenes.title: March Building
scenes.purpose: Chapter 4, line 1: Who walked, how old they were, how the villages received them, and how long the column became

narration.text: On 12 March 1930, Gandhi left Sabarmati with 78 volunteers. They walked for 24 days, 387 kilometres, through 48 villages.

scenes.title: Farmers Water Sample
scenes.purpose: Chapter 4, line 2: Who walked, how old they were, how the villages received them, and how long the column became

narration.text: The line grew. Farmers, weavers, students, women. The world's press came to watch a man walk toward the sea.

scenes.title: Seventy-eight Wall Sheets
scenes.purpose: Chapter 4, line 3: Who walked, how old they were, how the villages received them, and how long the column became

narration.text: The seventy-eight marchers came from almost every region, caste and creed.

scenes.title: Between Wall Sheets
scenes.purpose: Chapter 4, line 4: Who walked, how old they were, how the villages received them, and how long the column became

narration.text: Most of them were between twenty and thirty years old.

scenes.title: Cymbals Building
scenes.purpose: Chapter 4, line 5: Who walked, how old they were, how the villages received them, and how long the column became

narration.text: Villages met them with drums and cymbals as they passed.

scenes.title: Villages Building
scenes.purpose: Chapter 4, line 6: Who walked, how old they were, how the villages received them, and how long the column became

narration.text: They asked the villages for food and water to wash with, nothing more.

scenes.title: Kilometres Corridor
scenes.purpose: Chapter 4, line 7: Who walked, how old they were, how the villages received them, and how long the column became

narration.text: The column stretched at least three kilometres behind him.

scenes.title: April Plinth
scenes.purpose: Chapter 5, line 1: The handful of mud, the illegal salt, the telegrams and the greeting

narration.text: At 8:30 on the morning of 6 April, Gandhi bent down and picked up a lump of salt.

scenes.title: Within Plinth
scenes.purpose: Chapter 5, line 2: The handful of mud, the illegal salt, the telegrams and the greeting

narration.text: The law was broken. Within weeks, millions joined. Over 60,000 were jailed.

scenes.title: Empire Plinth
scenes.purpose: Chapter 5, line 3: The handful of mud, the illegal salt, the telegrams and the greeting

narration.text: He raised a lump of salty mud and said he was shaking the Empire's foundations.

scenes.title: Followers Flame
scenes.purpose: Chapter 5, line 4: The handful of mud, the illegal salt, the telegrams and the greeting

narration.text: He boiled seawater into illegal salt and told his followers to do the same.

scenes.title: Jalalpur Room
scenes.purpose: Chapter 5, line 5: The handful of mud, the illegal salt, the telegrams and the greeting

narration.text: About seven hundred telegrams went out from the post office at Jalalpur.

scenes.title: Sarojini Naidu Plinth
scenes.purpose: Chapter 5, line 6: The handful of mud, the illegal salt, the telegrams and the greeting

narration.text: Sarojini Naidu saluted him at Dandi as a law breaker.

scenes.title: Dharasana Wall Sheets
scenes.purpose: Chapter 6, line 1: The arrest, the raid, the beatings and the instruction not to resist

narration.text: Gandhi was arrested in a mango grove before the Dharasana raid began.

scenes.title: Dharasana Gate
scenes.purpose: Chapter 6, line 2: The arrest, the raid, the beatings and the instruction not to resist

narration.text: The Raj answered with lathis. At Dharasana, volunteers walked into the clubs and did not raise a hand.

scenes.title: Empire Gate
scenes.purpose: Chapter 6, line 3: The arrest, the raid, the beatings and the instruction not to resist

narration.text: The world saw the choice the Empire made. The story reached 1,350 newspapers.

scenes.title: Kasturba Gate
scenes.purpose: Chapter 6, line 4: The arrest, the raid, the beatings and the instruction not to resist

narration.text: A retired judge of seventy-six led the raid with Kasturba beside him.

scenes.title: Sarojini Naidu Gate
scenes.purpose: Chapter 6, line 5: The arrest, the raid, the beatings and the instruction not to resist

narration.text: Both were arrested, and Sarojini Naidu took command of the march.

scenes.title: Beaten Corridor
scenes.purpose: Chapter 6, line 6: The arrest, the raid, the beatings and the instruction not to resist

narration.text: She told them they would be beaten but must not raise a hand.

scenes.title: March Desk
scenes.purpose: Chapter 7, line 1: The pact, the terms, and the movement closed down by its own side

narration.text: In March 1931, Gandhi and Irwin signed a pact. Over 90,000 political prisoners were released.

scenes.title: Everything Desk
scenes.purpose: Chapter 7, line 2: The pact, the terms, and the movement closed down by its own side

narration.text: The Raj did not abolish the salt tax. The movement did not win everything. It won something harder to take away: a nation had seen its own power.

scenes.title: 1931 Administrator's Office
scenes.purpose: Chapter 7, line 3: The pact, the terms, and the movement closed down by its own side

narration.text: Gandhi was released in 1931 to meet Irwin on equal terms.

scenes.title: 1934 Flame
scenes.purpose: Chapter 7, line 4: The pact, the terms, and the movement closed down by its own side

narration.text: Congress ended satyagraha as official policy in 1934.

scenes.title: Empire Family Record
scenes.purpose: Chapter 8, line 1: What the world took from it, and the concession inside the Empire itself

narration.text: The Empire had armies. It had no answer to a man picking up salt.

scenes.title: Gandhi Family Record
scenes.purpose: Chapter 8, line 2: What the world took from it, and the concession inside the Empire itself

narration.text: Time magazine named Gandhi its Man of the Year for 1930.

scenes.title: England Flame
scenes.purpose: Chapter 8, line 3: What the world took from it, and the concession inside the Empire itself

narration.text: A provincial governor conceded that England could hold India only by consent.
